# Parametric bootstrap standard errors and confidence intervals

Simulates `n_boot` series of the same length from the fitted model,
refits each one, and summarizes the resulting sampling distribution of
the estimates. This is the recommended alternative to the Hessian
standard errors of
[`gs_fit()`](https://thiagodoregosousa.github.io/GEVStableGarch/reference/gs_fit.md)
when the asymptotic normal approximation is unreliable: near a boundary
(stable tail index near 2, GEV shape near \\\pm 0.5\\, APARCH asymmetry
near \\\pm 1\\) or, for GEV innovations, because the support depends on
the shape parameter and the usual regularity conditions do not hold
(Efron, 1979).

## Usage

``` r
gs_bootstrap(fit, n_boot = 199, level = 0.95, seed = NULL, ...)
```

## Arguments

- fit:

  A `gs_fit` object.

- n_boot:

  Number of bootstrap replications.

- level:

  Confidence level of the percentile intervals.

- seed:

  Optional seed for reproducibility.

- ...:

  Passed to
  [`gs_fit()`](https://thiagodoregosousa.github.io/GEVStableGarch/reference/gs_fit.md)
  (for example `algorithm`).

## Value

A list with `se` (named vector of bootstrap standard errors), `ci` (a
matrix with `lower` and `upper` percentile limits), `replicates` (the
`n_boot` by number-of-parameters matrix of estimates, failed fits as
`NA` rows), `n_fail` and `level`.

## Details

Each replication is refit with `hessian = FALSE`; replications whose fit
fails are dropped and counted in `n_fail`.

## References

Efron, B. (1979). Bootstrap methods: another look at the jackknife. The
Annals of Statistics, 7(1), 1-26.

## See also

[`gs_fit()`](https://thiagodoregosousa.github.io/GEVStableGarch/reference/gs_fit.md)

## Examples

``` r
# \donttest{
spec <- gs_spec(garch = c(1, 1), dist = gs_gev())
model <- gs_model(spec, mu = 0, omega = 0.1, alpha = 0.1, beta = 0.8,
                  dist_par = c(xi = 0.2))
x <- gs_sim(model, n = 800, seed = 1)$y
#> Warning: Persistence 1.2018 >= 1: the simulated scale has no stationary level.
fit <- gs_fit(x, spec)
#> Warning: Parameter(s) at a bound, standard errors set to NA: omega.
#> Warning: Persistence 1.2030 >= 1: E(sigma_t^delta) is not finite and long horizon scale forecasts diverge.
gs_bootstrap(fit, n_boot = 99, seed = 1)
#> $se
#>           mu        omega       alpha1        beta1           xi 
#> 9.628968e+14 9.005972e+32 2.045243e-01 1.436079e-01 5.473430e-02 
#> 
#> $ci

#> alpha1  1.059892e-01 8.636919e-01
#> beta1   2.630165e-01 7.776833e-01
#> xi     -1.422613e-02 2.029890e-01
#>
```
